goal.summary: Implement reusable capacity-aware MXFP8 C = A * B^T on the existing Buckyball MXMM Ball. Read project.json and deliver a callable implementation for matrices exceeding physical bank capacity, executed through the repository ISA and focused BEMU.
goal.deliverable: ball/ with applicable source patches, callable consumer, numerical checks and reproduction commands.
scope: MXMM host packing, tiling, ISA and focused verification.

Inputs are row-major E4M3 codes and per-row E8M0 scales per 32 K elements; output is FP32. Support M=1 or multiples of 16 up to 64, N positive multiples of 16 up to 80, K positive multiples of 32 up to 4096.
constraints: Use the pinned poly configuration and its actual bank capacities; preserve numerical semantics.
Expose dimensions and input data at the callable interface; do not hardcode case outputs. Repeated calls must not retain stale accumulator state.
Build and run actual RISC-V ELF on focused BEMU with the MXMM core selected.
project.json identifies the pinned baseline and optional BEMU/compiler references. Work in independent prepared checkouts and preserve the baseline for comparison.

criteria.statement: Using the pinned checkout, a callable implementation accepts dimensions and data and executes real MXMM instructions on focused BEMU. Respect active three-bank capacities, scales and output bases, DMA, K partitions and accumulation; a schedule or mathematical reference alone fails.

For every vector defined by the frozen case seed and dataRule, independently rebuild and compare target FP32 outputs with a decoded-input reference. Cover signed and zero codes, finite scales, long-K accumulation, M/N output tiling, repeated calls and output guards. Require exact results when representable and measured error bounds otherwise.
Reproduce existing MXMM capacity/window/chain regressions and tests for every changed boundary. Record actual terminal results and distinguish BEMU evidence from RTL correctness.

Freeze ball/ with all patches, source identities, callable input/output layout, numerical rules and commands needed for a fresh reviewer to reproduce inputs and outputs without worker workspaces or build outputs. Report remaining gaps.
